summary: PrfTraining is a user control facilitating staff training management, allowing administrators to view, add, edit, and delete training records for staff. Its interface comprises multiple ASP.NET web controls, data sources, and validation logic. The control supports both data entry and workflow for training records, handling user permissions dynamically.
purpose: The purpose of PrfTraining is to enable authorized users (typically administrators) to manage staff training records efficiently through a web interface, including CRUD operations, validations, and workflow behaviors.

workflows.name: Add Training Record
steps: User clicks 'Add' button or 'Add Empty Data'.
Cache and redirect to current page.

workflows.name: Edit Training Record
steps: Cache and redirect to current page.

business_rules: Only SystemAdministrator or LocalAdministrator can view/edit certain fields (e.g., Notes, Trainer, Approved, LateCancellation, TrainedWith).
Editable fields and Add/Edit/Delete actions are conditioned by ScreenIsEditable and data.Editable.
validations: Form must be Page.IsValid for insert/update (otherwise operation is canceled).
Notes textbox enforces a max length of 200 characters.
TrainingCodeID, CourseCodeID, TrainerCodeID must be selected (default to '0' if not).
DurationHours defaults to -1 if not provided.
conditions: Fields/controls visibility depends on user role (SystemAdministrator or LocalAdministrator).
Fields are disabled in non-edit mode.
EmptyData panel is visible if GridView has no rows and ScreenIsEditable.
system_behavior: On row data bound, certain fields are greyed out if LateCancellation is set.
Modal popup details are shown for Add/Edit.
Redirection after insert/update/delete to maintain current page state.
Dropdowns preselect values based on data.
exceptions: If UserSession is null, data selection is canceled.
JavaScript errors in EmptyDataTemplate handled by custom workflow (not Grid.cs).
content_gaps: Underlying data model for StaffTraining entity is not fully described.

No information on error handling for database failures.
Some modal and grid behaviors rely on external classes (e.g., Grid, Dropdown, CalendarExtender) not illustrated here.
